title: Buffon–Barbier: Discharging the Integrability Hypothesis from Smoothness
description: Removes the explicit integrability hypothesis (hInnerInt) from the Buffon–Barbier smooth-curve theorem of buffons-needle-oq-01-oq-01. Using the already-proved angular-average identity, the inner angular integral is shown to equal 2‖γ'(·)‖ pointwise, so continuity of the derivatives makes it continuous and hence interval-integrable. The headline result establishes the full Buffon–Barbier formula E[crossings] = 2L/(πd) for any C¹ curve with no integrability, Fubini, or differentiability side-conditions.

meta.author: Barbier (1860); Lean formalization 2026

The derivative of a C¹ function is continuous

overview.historicalContext: The parent entry buffons-needle-oq-01-oq-01 proves the Buffon–Barbier smooth-curve formula E[crossings] = 2L/(πd), but its main theorems (buffon_smooth_concrete, buffon_smooth_full) carry an explicit integrability hypothesis hInnerInt on the inner angular integral, viewed as a function of the curve parameter t. Its listed open question #2 asks whether hInnerInt can be derived from the smoothness of γ rather than assumed. This file answers YES.
overview.problemStatement:
**Open Question from buffons-needle-oq-01-oq-01**: Can the integrability hypothesis
  hInnerInt : IntervalIntegrable (fun t => ∫ θ in 0..π, |γ'ₓ(t)·sin θ + γ'ᵧ(t)·cos θ|) volume a b
be proved from smoothness of γ, instead of being carried as an explicit assumption?

**Answer**: YES. The inner integral, as a function of t, is exactly 2‖γ'(t)‖ (by the angular-average theorem), which is continuous whenever γ' is continuous; a continuous function is interval-integrable. Consequently the Buffon–Barbier formula holds for any C¹ curve with no analytic side-conditions.
overview.text: Removes the integrability hypothesis from the Buffon–Barbier smooth-curve theorem by observing that the inner angular integral equals 2‖γ'(·)‖ pointwise, so continuity of the derivatives gives interval-integrability for free.
overview.proofStrategy:
**Key observation**: The angular-average identity ∫_0^π |a·sin θ + b·cos θ| dθ = 2√(a²+b²) — already proved in the parent file for *every* (a,b) — applies pointwise at (γ'ₓ(t), γ'ᵧ(t)). Hence the inner-integral function equals
  t ↦ 2√(γ'ₓ(t)² + γ'ᵧ(t)²) = 2‖γ'(t)‖.

**Discharging integrability**:
1. innerIntegral_eq: funext + angular_average gives the equality of functions.
2. innerIntegral_continuous(On): 2‖γ'(·)‖ is continuous whenever γ'ₓ, γ'ᵧ are, since √ and the arithmetic operations preserve continuity.
3. hInnerInt_of_continuous(On): continuity ⟹ interval-integrability (ContinuousOn.intervalIntegrable).

**Removing the hypothesis**: Feeding the discharged hypothesis into the parent's buffon_smooth_full yields buffon_smooth_of_continuous(On) — the formula with hInnerInt gone.

**Headline (C¹)**: ContDiff ℝ 1 supplies both HasDerivAt at every point (ContDiff.differentiable) and continuity of the derivative (ContDiff.continuous_deriv), so buffon_smooth_of_contDiff establishes E[crossings] = 2L/(πd) for any C¹ curve with no integrability, Fubini, or differentiability side-conditions.
keyInsights: The integrability hypothesis was never an independent assumption: it is a pointwise consequence of the angular-average identity the parent already proves.
The inner angular integral, as a function of the curve parameter, is literally twice the speed 2‖γ'(t)‖ — the arc-length integrand up to a factor of 2.
Continuity of a function on uIcc a b is enough for interval-integrability (ContinuousOn.intervalIntegrable), so no measure-theoretic estimate is needed.
C¹ is exactly the right smoothness hypothesis: it yields both the pointwise differentiability and the continuity of the derivative that the theorem needs.
After this reduction, the only genuine analytic input in the whole Buffon–Barbier chain is the angular-average identity itself — never a separate integrability side-condition.
prerequisites: Continuity of composite functions and Real.sqrt

sections.summary: buffon_smooth_of_contDiff establishes E[crossings] = 2L/(πd) for any C¹ curve, discharging every analytic side-condition from the single hypothesis that γ is continuously differentiable.

conclusion.summary: The integrability hypothesis hInnerInt of the parent Buffon–Barbier formalization is not an independent assumption but a pointwise consequence of the angular-average identity: the inner angular integral equals 2‖γ'(·)‖, which is continuous — hence interval-integrable — whenever the derivatives are continuous. The headline theorem establishes the Buffon–Barbier formula for any C¹ curve with no analytic side-conditions at all.
conclusion.implications:
**1. A cleaner statement of Buffon–Barbier.** buffon_smooth_of_contDiff states the classical theorem under its natural hypothesis (γ is C¹) with no auxiliary integrability, Fubini, or differentiability conditions leaking into the signature.

**2. Integrability was hiding in the angular average.** The reduction makes explicit that the only analytic content of the smooth-curve case is the identity ∫_0^π |a sin θ + b cos θ| dθ = 2√(a²+b²); once that is proved, both the value of the integral and its integrability-in-t come for free.

**3. Toward full axiom elimination in BuffonsNoodle.lean.** With hInnerInt discharged, the remaining obstacle to removing the axioms in BuffonsNoodle.lean is purely definitional bookkeeping between concreteSmoothExpectedCrossings and the axiomatic smoothExpectedCrossings.
